messages:
Maya: @here seeing repeated GPU attach failures in eu-west3 this morning. correlated with a salvage sweep running on scratchpool; node iops jumped from ~12k to ~72k and the GPU provisioning queue stalled. sample log: `gnode-eu-west3-11 nvme0 iops=72000 read_lat_ms=25`

infra-bot: Scheduled job started: janitor.salvage on gnode-eu-west3-11 at 07:14:02 UTC (job-id: salvage-2026-03-20-0714) :robot_face:

Jonathan: Is this the new "salvage-sweep" schedule? we rolled that out last week to reclaim stale ephemeral blobs, right?

Maya: yes, rollout happened last Wed. Seems the job isn't honoring any iops budget; it does wide-range reads and spikes the local NVMe. Happens right into our batch/gpu-attach window (07:00-08:00).

Lee: we only configured `janitor.sweep.concurrency=8` which limits goroutines, not IO throughput. We should add an explicit iops cap and a cooperative backoff. propose: `janitor.sweep.max_iops=8000` and exponential backoff on read failures.

Sasha: +1. Immediate mitigation: can we mark nodes in eu-west3 as no-gpu-attach until the sweep finishes? That will prevent new attach attempts from queueing and timing out. Devon can you patch autoscaler/pool policy? :pray: 

Devon: On it. I'll deploy a short-lived policy patch to disable attaches for the eu-west3 scratch pool for ~20m, and add a rate-limiter to the janitor. Patch snippet I'll push: 

```
# janitor config (canary)
sweep:
  max_iops: 8000
  backoff_ms: 250
  concurrency: 4
```

Jonathan: We should also add per-node iops telemetry for janitor jobs (histograms + 1m/5m alerts). Right now we only see aggregate cleaner throughput which hides hotspots.

Maya: After disabling attach, provisioning recovered and GPU queues drained. Proposed action items: 1) add iops cap + backoff to janitor, 2) move salvage schedule off-peak (e.g., 02:00-03:30), 3) add alert if janitor-induced node iops > 10k for >5m, 4) postmortem note in eng-infra and eng-sre if recurrence.

Devon: I'll open a quick PR for the config change and the autoscaler patch. Will post link here when created.

Sasha: Can we also estimate cost impact? wide-range reads on NVMe amplify wear and might increase downstream reads for any attached GC/replication jobs. Might not be huge $ but operational risk is higher.

Jonathan: rough ballpark: one salvage sweep on a hot node produced ~2TB read amplification in 30m; if that repeats across 100 nodes it adds carrier IO and increases chance of transient corruption. We should throttle before scale.

Maya: Agreed. Thanks everyone for the quick mitigation. Keeping thread open for the PR link and a short follow-up runbook for future salvage runs.

Devon: PR: https://git.internal.redwood/pr/infra/4321 (canary config + autoscaler attach-disable). I'll roll canary at 07:40 UTC and watch metrics.

Maya: Got it. I'll check histograms and reopen if we see residual read tail. :thumbsup:
